claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 in the as-synthesized state has a hierarchical heterostructure with measurable variations at multiple length scales.
Explicitly incorporating grain boundaries, heterogeneous phase distributions, and sub-grain structures into the model will improve predictions relative to a homogenized model.
The enriched model will predict Young's modulus under tensile loading with at least 10% higher accuracy.
The enriched model will predict yield strength under tensile loading with at least 10% higher accuracy.
The enriched model will predict fracture behavior with at least 10% higher accuracy.
The enriched model will provide approximately 50% faster computational turnaround than conventional homogenized simulations.
The distribution and connectivity of micro- and mesoscale phases constitute the relevant structural mediator.
Grain boundaries and secondary phases in the heterostructure act as sites for dislocation nucleation.
Grain boundaries and secondary phases in the heterostructure contribute to crack arrest.
Accounting for detailed microstructural heterogeneity enables the model to capture stress distributions more accurately.
Accounting for detailed microstructural heterogeneity enables the model to capture localized yielding, failure initiation, and crack propagation more accurately.
More accurate representation of stress and failure processes will increase correlation between simulated and experimentally observed mechanical behavior.
Targeted modeling of critical microstructural regions and improved convergence will reduce simulation time by approximately 50%.
Conventional homogenized simulations require longer computational times than the proposed microstructure-enriched model.
Conventional homogenized simulations have higher prediction errors than the proposed microstructure-enriched model.
The proposed advantage may disappear when the hierarchical heterostructure is insufficiently pronounced.
Uncharacterized processing defects may prevent the proposed model from achieving its predicted advantage.
High temperature or high strain rate may activate different deformation mechanisms and invalidate the proposed predictive advantage.
